title: Find the minimal state
prompt:
The Watchlist gets two new features. Each movie can now have a star rating from 1 to 5 that you set by clicking stars, and a dropdown lets you sort the list by **title** or by **year**. The header also shows the average rating of the movies you've watched.

**Which of these should be stored in state?** Pick every one that is truly state; leave out anything that's derived.
hints: For each item, ask: can I calculate this from other data I already have?
An average, a sorted copy and a yes/no about the sort can all be computed from the ratings and the chosen sort order.
explanation: Only two things change on their own because of what the user does: each movie's rating (stored on the movie in the movies state) and the chosen sort order. Everything else is calculated during render. The average is `watched ratings ÷ count`, the sorted list is a sorted copy of the movies based on the sort order, and "is sorted by year" is just `sortOrder === 'year'`. Storing any of those would create a second copy that can go stale.

ratings.text: Each movie's rating, stored as a field on the movie in the movies state
ratings.why: Correct. A rating changes when the user clicks a star and can't be computed from anything else.

average-rating.text: The average rating shown in the header
average-rating.why: Derived. Compute it from the watched movies' ratings during render, or it will drift when a rating changes.

sort-order.why: Correct. It changes when the user picks from the dropdown, and nothing else can tell you what they picked.

sorted-movies.text: A sorted copy of the movie list
sorted-movies.why: Derived. Sort a copy of the movies by the current sort order while rendering; storing it means re-sorting by hand after every change.

is-sorted-by-year.text: A boolean `isSortedByYear` used to style the dropdown
is-sorted-by-year.why: Derived. It's `sortOrder === 'year'`. Keeping it in its own state lets it disagree with the actual sort order.
